 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous 2nd Bail Application No. 13051/2024 Heeralal S/o Shri Naji @ Nanji, Aged About 47 Years, R/o Gopa Ki Bhagal Pachoriya, P.s. Knod, Dist. Udaipur,raj.

(Presently Lodged In Dist. Jail, Udaipur)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Ms. Shewta Sand  Mr. P.L. Maru
Mr. Ramdev Rajpurohit For Respondent(s) : Mr. Lalit Kishore Sen, Dy.G.A.
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 11/11/2024 1.
The jurisdiction of this court has been invoked by way of filing the instant second bail application under Section 439 CrPC at the instance of accused-petitioner.

The requisite details of the matter are tabulated herein below:
S.No. Particulars of the Case  2. Concerned Police Station Kanod  3. District Udaipur  4. Offences alleged in the FIR Section 376 of the IPC

5 . Offences added, if any Section 376(2)(l), 354,
366 and 450 of the IPC  6. Date of passing of impugned 30.09.2023  order Heeralal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45979) on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18184489/
1 2.
It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.

There are no factors at play in the [2024:RJ-JD:45979] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-13051/2024] case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused- petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have heard and considered the submissions made by both the parties and perused the material available on record.
5. The petitioner was arrested in this case on 09.06.2023 and now more than one year elapsed; he is languishing in jail.
The allegations that the victim who is 20 years old, is of poor brain has not been supported with any concrete evidence till now.
The fact remains that she has passed 7 th standard with average marks.

She has been interrogated by the learned Magistrate during investigation on 10.07.2023 and whereafter a note was put thereon that she was able to understand the questions and to reply adequately and whereafter, she had narrated the incident.

6. The important aspect of the matter is that when she was examined by the Medical Officer on 08.6.2023, the Doctor examined her has specifically noted that her hymen was imperforated meaning thereby there was no harm to her hymen.
P.W. 3 Savita has been examined in the trial.

Interestingly, the victim does not state in her statement that when the sexual assault was made by the petitioner upon her, the witness Savita came there, on the contrary, P.W. 3 child 'S' states that when she went on the spot, she made rescue to her aunt.

7. Be that as it may, taking into account the fact that deficiency of evidence with regard to insanity of the victim, so also looking to her ability to understand the things and her age of discretion so also taking into account a conflict between medical and ocular evidence as well as the period of incarceration I deem it just and appropriate to allow the instant bail application.
8. It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

9. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
